Pointer focus draws no ring; keyboard focus shows Arc's shared focus ring. The focused scrubber fills and enlarges its thumb.
motion: The first time the block scrolls into view, the head travels every month and the path draws in behind it; the dotted future path, arrows and labels fade in once it lands.

Scrubbing moves the head along the real curve, not a straight line between months. A press glides the head to the pointer once, then it follows one to one, and a release settles on the nearest month with the smooth spring, which never overshoots.
Switching channel morphs every point, arrow and the path itself on the smooth spring; the readout numbers count through the in between values and month labels crossfade.
Every moving part (path, trail length, head, guides, dots, arrows, scrubber thumb and readout values) is a motion value written once per frame, so none of it re-renders React.
Reduced motion shows the finished path at once, jumps the head to each month, steps playback month by month and swaps channels without a morph.

name: contact-section
title: Contact section
description: A validated contact form that morphs into a confirmation, support channels, and office cards with local times.
whenToUse: Contact pages and sections on marketing sites.
Sales or support pages that list several channels with response times.
Companies with offices in several time zones.
whenNotToUse: Use support-widget for an in-app help launcher.
Use signup-form or login blocks for account flows.
accessibility: Fields use labelled Arc Input and Textarea; errors appear after the first submit and update as you type.
A failed send shows a role="alert" message and keeps the form.
Office open status is written out, not shown by color alone.
motion: The form card springs into the confirmation; faces slide along one axis in the direction of travel out of a soft blur.
The topic highlight glides between chips.
Reduced motion swaps faces without travel.

name: credit-topup
title: Credit top-up
description: A card for buying AI credits. It shows the balance with a 14 day usage chart and how many days are left, three preset packs with bonus badges, a custom amount slider with a live price, auto top-up with a threshold and the saved Visa or Mastercard. When you buy, the new balance rolls in like an odometer.
whenToUse: Selling prepaid AI credits or tokens with volume bonuses.
A billing settings section where people also manage auto top-up and their card.
An out of credits moment where the balance, burn rate and a one click refill belong together.
whenNotToUse: Subscription plan changes with seats and billing cycles: use a plan picker or checkout-live.
Collecting a new card number: use a card form or a hosted payment element, then pass the saved card here.
Read-only usage reporting: use a usage meter or a chart.
accessibility: Packs and thresholds are radio groups with roving focus and labels that read the amount, price and bonus, such as "5,000 credits, $50, 10% bonus".
Rolling numerals are aria-hidden; a visually hidden copy of each value is read instead, so screen readers never hear partial digits.
A polite live region announces the charge, the result ("Added 5,500 credits. Nothing was charged.") and errors. Without onPurchase it says the checkout is simulated.
Balance health is an icon plus a label (Running low, Healthy), never color alone. The usage chart is one image with a spoken summary.
The Buy button stays focusable while processing (aria-busy) so keyboard focus is not lost.
motion: After a purchase the balance rolls up odometer style over 0.9s: each digit rolls one way to its target and the lower places take one extra lap, so it reads as counting. New leading places open their width on a bounce-free spring.
The total and price roll in 0.24s as the slider moves, in tabular numerals so nothing shifts.
The pack selection ring and threshold pill glide between options on a 0.24s spring with no bounce. Status, health, days left and the saved card crossfade (100ms out, 160ms in, 2px rise).
The card never changes size between idle, processing, done and error.
Reduced motion: numbers and highlights jump to their end state; crossfades stay as plain fades.

name: cta-section
title: CTA section
description: A call to action as a centered closing section, a split beside a setup card that completes itself, or a dismissible banner.
whenToUse: The last section of a landing page, asking for a trial or demo.
An in-page prompt beside a product visual that shows the outcome.
A slim promotional banner above content.
whenNotToUse: The first screen of a page. Use Hero section.
Collecting an email. Use Newsletter signup.
A persistent site-wide notice. Use Announcement bar.
accessibility: Each variant is a section labelled by its heading.
Actions with href are real links; others are buttons. Simulated confirmations announce politely.
The dismiss button has the name "Dismiss"; the banner closes its gap so focus order stays clean.
The setup card is aria-hidden: the copy beside it carries the message.
motion: Primary actions lean their arrow forward on hover; buttons press to .97 and morph their width when the label changes.
Split: the stage rises into view once, then the setup card ticks its three steps, fills its progress line, and slides in teammates' faces.
Banner: dismissing fades it, scales it to .98, and springs its height closed so the page below moves up smoothly.
Reduced motion shows the finished setup card and removes travel.

name: customer-galaxy
title: Customer galaxy
description: 2,400 accounts as a drifting galaxy that spirals into clusters by plan, region or health.
whenToUse: Customer success or revenue pages to explore where MRR and risk concentrate.
Showcase views that cluster thousands of accounts by plan, region, or health.
whenNotToUse: Use customers-table when people need to find and act on specific accounts.
Use semantic-zoom for hierarchical data like teams and projects.
Use bar-chart for simple totals by segment.
accessibility: The stage is role="application" with a roledescription, a text summary label and a keyboard hint.
Grouping uses a tablist and tabpanel; cluster rows are aria-pressed buttons with MRR and risk in their labels.
Zoom buttons have labels, and a polite live region announces selections.
motion: Accounts drift, then spiral into clusters with spring physics when grouping changes; flying to a cluster eases the camera.
The tab pill slides with a shared layout spring, and panel rows reorder with layout animation.
Reduced motion is passed to the engine, which snaps to layouts, and UI transitions become instant.

name: delivery-tracker
title: Delivery tracker
description: A live order tracker whose marker glides between stops while the arrival time rolls.
whenToUse: Order status pages that follow a delivery from dispatch to door.
Tracking screens with a live arrival time and an event history.
Deliveries where people can message or call the courier.
whenNotToUse: Use timeline for a static list of past events.
Use progress when a single percentage is enough.
Use support-conversation for a full chat with support.
accessibility: Stage changes and arrival updates are announced through a polite live region.
Quick replies are a labelled group, and the courier typing indicator is a role="status" with a label.
Call status text updates in its own polite live region.
motion: The marker glides between stops while the arrival time rolls.
The contact button morphs into the contact panel through a shared layoutId.
Reduced motion makes the marker and panel morph instant.

name: docs-sidebar
title: Docs sidebar
description: A docs layout with a live filtering nav tree, version switcher, and a gliding on this page outline.
whenToUse: Product or API documentation with a nav tree and page outline.
Docs that need a version switcher and a filterable tree.
Pages where the on this page outline should follow scroll.
whenNotToUse: Use tree-view for a plain hierarchy outside a docs layout.
Use sidebar-rail for app navigation.
Use command-palette for global search across docs.
accessibility: The rail toggle exposes aria-expanded and aria-keyshortcuts="[".
Filter results are announced as a count in a polite status region.
The nav tree supports arrow key movement from the search field into the list.
motion: The outline indicator glides to the heading in view, and the sidebar folds to a rail on a spring.
Nav groups expand by height as the filter opens matching branches.
Reduced motion makes the glide and folds instant.

name: document-extract
title: Document extraction
description: Turns a document into typed data with a model and shows where every value came from: fields fill in as the page is read, and hovering a value lights its source on the PDF.
whenToUse: Accounts payable, logistics or back office tools that turn invoices, receipts, emails or forms into records a person accepts before saving.
Any extraction flow where a reviewer needs to see exactly where each value came from and fix the few the model was unsure about.
Demos and settings pages for a structured output feature, with the schema and live typed JSON one tab away.
whenNotToUse: Use ai-answer for a written answer with citations rather than typed fields.
Use knowledge-base to search and cite across many documents instead of reading one.
Use ai-inline-edit to rewrite text in place rather than pull values out of it.
Use agent-approvals when the decision is approving an agent's actions, not reviewing extracted values.
accessibility: The run's state is announced through a polite status region: extracting, done with how many fields need a check, failed with the error, and stopped. Checking a value and accepting speak through a second polite region, including that the preview only simulates the hand-off.

Confidence is a percent with an icon for every state that matters: a warning for low confidence, a check once checked or accepted, a pencil once edited. Spoken text reads the state and percent, and a flagged value's reason is tied to its input with aria-describedby.
Every value is a real input with a label. Table cells are inputs inside a table role with column headers, and each cell's name includes its column, row and whether it needs a check.
The viewer is a labeled region that announces its zoom; icon buttons have names and tooltips, and Fit reports its pressed state. The document switcher is a menu of radio items.
The connector, the scan bar and the confidence bars are decorative and hidden from assistive technology; the linked field, its status text and the summary carry the same information.

Values that do not fit their type, such as a date that is not YYYY-MM-DD or an IBAN whose check digits fail, show a message tied to the field, become null in the JSON, and block Accept all with a spoken reason.
Pointer focus draws no ring; keyboard focus shows Arc's shared focus ring. Inputs show focus with their border.
motion: The connector is one cubic Bezier that draws in over 220ms with round caps in the field's series color; a soft band of light travels along it once, then the line rests. Round anchors sit at both ends and the far one settles in as the line reaches it. It is measured on requestAnimationFrame while shown, so it follows scrolling, zoom and resizing without lag, and fades out in 120ms.

While extracting, one thin bar of light with a soft trailing fade passes down the page once. Each cited span takes a brief stronger tint as its value lands, then rests at a faint tint; the field's text fades in.
Zoom eases on the smooth spring around the middle of the canvas, so the point you are reading stays put.
Accept all turns each field's status into a check with a short stagger and a crisp snappy pop, and the footer bars turn green in the same order.

Table rows grow in on the smooth spring; reasons for flagged values open and close their height on the same spring. Status lines crossfade (out in 100ms, in over 160ms) inside a container that animates its height. Average confidence and cost roll on a short tween with tabular numerals.
Reduced motion removes the scan bar, the draw, the sheen, the cascade, flashes and tweens. Selection, tints, the connector, labels and announcements stay, and zoom changes in one step.

name: domain-verify
title: Domain verify
description: A custom domain setup card where customers add a domain and copy the DNS records. A live checker then polls resolvers, marks each record valid, not found or misconfigured with a one-line fix, and finishes with the domain verified and the SSL certificate issued.
whenToUse: Letting customers serve an app, docs site, status page or storefront from their own domain.
Verifying a sending domain for email (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) before turning on delivery.
Any setup step where a person must copy values into a third party and wait for propagation.
whenNotToUse: Buying or searching domains: use a search field with results instead.
Managing many domains at once: use a table with one row per domain and open this card per domain.
One-off copy of a single value: a copy-button next to the value is enough.
accessibility: The card is a labelled section; the records are a list labelled DNS records.
A polite live region announces each step (added, checking, needs a fix, verified, certificate issued) and adds "Simulated, no DNS was queried" when no verify handler is passed.
Status is never color alone: every record and the domain show an icon with a short label.
The domain field is labelled, marks itself aria-invalid on a bad domain and is described by the footer status.
Placeholder rows behind the empty state are inert, so their copy buttons are skipped by keyboard and screen readers.
Each copy button has its own label, such as "Copy TXT value", and announces the copy.
motion: Text and icon swaps are single crossfades: the old one fades out in 100ms, the new one fades in over 160ms with a 2px rise.
Rows fade in over 160ms with a 40ms stagger when the records arrive. No row, column or slot changes size between states.
When a fix hint wraps on a narrow card, the card eases to its measured height on a spring with no bounce.
Checking rows show a steady spinner, and the footer label carries a calm shimmer while checks run.
Reduced motion keeps every state and label, swaps instantly and stops the spinner. The demo loop pauses off screen.

name: empty-states
title: Empty states
description: Four empty states in one illustration whose shapes morph between scenes as you switch tabs.
whenToUse: A reference for no results, offline, inbox zero, and 404 moments with one shared illustration style.
Extracting one scene as a richer empty state for a key screen.
whenNotToUse: Use empty-state for a simple empty state with an icon, text, and action.
Use onboarding-illustration for first-run screens that teach the product.
Use skeleton while content is still loading.
accessibility: Scenes use role="tablist", "tab" and "tabpanel" with aria-selected and aria-controls.
The illustration is a role="img" labelled by the scene; a polite live region reports action results.
motion: Each shape morphs its path to the next scene with slight per-shape delays, and the tab indicator glides with a layoutId.
Reduced motion swaps scenes with a short fade and no morph.

name: env-variables
title: Environment variables
description: An environment variables and secrets manager with masked values, per-environment scope toggles, .env paste import with duplicate and invalid key warnings, write-only sensitive values, an environment diff by fingerprint, and a redeploy banner.
whenToUse: A settings screen where developers manage configuration and secrets across development, preview, and production.
Onboarding a project by pasting an existing .env file and scoping it to environments in one step.
Auditing drift between environments before a release, such as a key set in Preview but missing in Production.
whenNotToUse: Use api-keys for creating, scoping, and revoking access tokens that your product issues to its users.
Use a plain form for a handful of fixed settings that are not per environment.
accessibility: Masked values render as bullets hidden from assistive technology plus a visually hidden "Hidden value" or "Sensitive value, write-only" label; the real value is only rendered after Reveal.
Reveal and environment toggles are buttons with aria-pressed and names that include the key, such as "Production for DATABASE_URL".
Each row's toggles sit in a labelled group; the wide matrix column heads are decorative and every toggle carries its own name.
Inline errors (invalid key, key already set in an environment, empty value) are tied to their fields; scope conflicts appear as an alert under the row.
A polite live region announces every change, import, removal, and redeploy result, and the .env parse summary updates live as you type.
Pointer focus draws no ring; keyboard focus shows Arc's shared focus ring. Keyboard position shows as a fill on toggles and icon buttons, matching hover.
motion: The redeploy banner, add panel, inline editor, and conflict notes open with height and opacity on the smooth spring and close with a quicker exit ease.
Environment toggles fill with a snappy scale and draw their check with pathLength, both without overshoot.
Revealing a value crossfades the mask and the value with a short rise in a fixed height slot, so the row never jumps.
Added and removed rows grow and collapse their height so the list closes its gap; saved or imported rows glow once in the accent and fade.
The Variables and Compare views crossfade with a small rise. Reduced motion removes all travel and lands every change at once.

name: eval-suite
title: Eval suite
description: Run an evaluation suite on a new version of an LLM feature against its baseline: results stream in case by case, and regressions and fixes are called out with the cases behind them.
whenToUse: Regression testing an LLM feature before shipping a new prompt, model or agent version.
CI style eval dashboards where people need the overall score, the per category picture and the exact cases that broke in one place.
Triage of failing cases with an LLM judge: read both outputs, check the rubric, then accept the change or file an issue.
whenNotToUse: Use prompt-studio to edit a prompt and try it on one test case at a time.
Use model-arena for a blind side by side vote between models on a single prompt.
Use agent-run to follow one agent run step by step rather than scoring a suite.
Use token-inspector to look at token level probabilities of a single reply.
accessibility: Each category row is one image with a full text summary (passed, failed, errors, not yet scored, percent and the change against the baseline), so the 120 cells never become 120 announcements.
Outcomes never rely on color: pass, fail and error each have their own glyph, a regression is the only solid cell, and every list row spells out both outcomes in hidden text.
Case rows with a drilldown are buttons with aria-expanded and aria-controls; the drilldown is a labelled region. Rows without one are plain text.
The case filter is a radio group with roving focus. The run history is a slider whose value text names the run, its score and date.
Run start, finish (score, delta, regressions, improvements), stop, failure and each triage are announced in a polite status region, including when a run or an issue is simulated.
The score and every category percent count with tabular numerals; hidden text carries the final value so screen readers never read a number mid count.
Pointer focus draws no ring; keyboard focus shows Arc's shared focus ring.
motion: Cells fill as results arrive: the background tints over 240ms and the glyph scales in from 40 percent with an ease out. Cases in flight breathe once a second.
The score, category percents and cost count to their values on a critically damped spring, so a burst of results reads as one smooth count; a new run resets them at once.
Bars fill with a clip-path tween and tint green or red only when the run finishes; the deltas fade up 3px at the same moment.
The current run lands on the sparkline as a short drawn segment and a dot that scales in after it.

Rows that appear mid run, the drilldown and Show more open on the smooth spring with no overshoot. The filter highlight glides on a critically damped spring and the list height follows the new filter.
Run, Stop and Run again crossfade in place while the pill width follows the measured label.
Reduced motion fills cells, numbers, bars and panels immediately, stops the breathing, and keeps every state and announcement.

name: exploded-view
title: Exploded view
description: A scroll driven exploded view where a live phone screen built from five CSS 3D layers lies back, separates in depth with labels that follow each layer, takes each layer into focus, and then reassembles.
whenToUse: A showpiece section that shows a product is built with care, by literally taking its screen apart.
Explaining the layers of a design system or UI kit: tokens, grid, content, controls and overlays.
A launch page moment between the hero and the feature list, where one strong scroll interaction earns its place.
whenNotToUse: Use zoom-into-ui to fly into parts of a flat product screen and explain features in place.
Use scroll-story when the story is a sequence of product states rather than the structure of one screen.
Use a static screenshot or feature-illustration where scroll driven motion would compete with nearby sections.
accessibility: The section is labelled by its heading, and in container mode the scrolling frame is a focusable region named after it.
The 3D stage and its floating labels are decorative and hidden from assistive tech; an ordered list outside the stage names every layer with its caption, bottom to top.
The caption for the current stop sits in a polite live region, so each layer's name and description is announced as it takes focus.
Each stop is a real button with the stop's name as its label and aria-current="step" on the current one.

Pointer focus draws no ring; keyboard focus shows Arc's shared focus ring. A focused or hovered stop button fills with the muted surface, and the current stop's tick turns the accent and thickens, so position never depends on color alone.
motion: One scroll timeline drives everything: the screen tilts back and turns, the layers spread apart in depth, the labels draw their leader lines and fade in bottom to top, then the stack closes and stands up again.
Scroll progress is smoothed by a critically damped spring with no overshoot, so the stack follows the wheel softly, never passes its true position, and reverses mid way without a jump.

The layer in focus keeps full strength while the others step back in opacity, and its outline and label take the accent; the caption crossfades with a short rise on the enter curve and leaves faster than it arrives.

Labels live in flat stage space and are positioned each frame by projecting the layer's anchor point through the same rotation and perspective as the CSS, so text never tilts and the leader line always meets its layer.
Per frame work writes transforms and opacity straight to the DOM from the motion value; React renders only when the stop changes.
Reduced motion removes all travel: the screen shows flat at the start and end and fully separated for the five layer stops, switching instantly, and caption changes are instant.

name: faq-section
title: FAQ section
description: FAQs as an accordion, a topic rail, or a searchable list that highlights matches.
whenToUse: FAQ sections on pricing, product, and support pages.
Long FAQs that benefit from categories or live search.
whenNotToUse: Use accordion for generic collapsible content that is not a question list.
Use a docs page when answers need code, images, or long structure.
accessibility: Questions are buttons with aria-expanded controlling their answer region.
Search matches are wrapped in mark elements; closed items that match only in the answer show a short excerpt.
The search variant uses Arc SearchField with a real label.
motion: Answers open with height and opacity together and the plus icon turns.
Filtering and category changes move remaining items with layout animation.
Reduced motion opens and filters instantly.

name: feature-bento
title: Feature bento
description: A six cell feature bento where small, real product UI acts each feature out on hover.
whenToUse: A landing page features section that should show the product rather than list it.
Launch pages where each capability has one clear, demonstrable behavior.
whenNotToUse: Long feature lists or comparison tables. Use Plan comparison.
A guided walkthrough with order. Use Scroll story.
Cards that open into detail. Use Spotlight grid.
accessibility: The section is labelled by its heading; each cell is a list item with a real h3 and paragraph.
Illustrations are aria-hidden: they repeat what the title and sentence already say.
With href, the title is the only link and its hit area stretches over the cell, so there is one tab stop per cell.
Focusing a linked cell plays its illustration, the same as hovering it.
motion: Cells rise 14px and fade in once as they enter view, staggered by column.

With a mouse, hovering a cell acts its feature out: a cursor drags a selection while another types, a palette highlight glides to its match, the latest bar lifts and takes the accent, steps check off along a filling line, a switch flips and saves, a scrubber slides back and the text swaps to that version.
Hover in uses the shared spring curve with small sequenced delays; hover out returns quickly with no delays.
On touch screens each cell plays once when it scrolls into view and stays in its end state.
Only transform and opacity animate, plus two tiny typing reveals. Reduced motion jumps straight to each state.

name: feature-voting
title: Feature voting
description: A public feature request board where votes roll digit by digit and the button fills with the accent. Top, New and Trending reorder the rows with one smooth move. A built-in composer suggests similar requests as you type, so people vote instead of posting duplicates.
whenToUse: A public feature request page where customers vote and suggest ideas.
An in-app Give feedback panel that shows what is planned and shipped.
A customer portal that needs to deflect duplicate requests before they are posted.
whenNotToUse: A full roadmap with columns per stage: use a kanban style board.
One off feedback on a single page or screen: use a short feedback form.
Release notes of what already shipped: use changelog-feed.
accessibility: Vote buttons are toggle buttons (aria-pressed) labelled with the request and its count, for example Vote for SAML single sign-on with Okta, 351 votes.
Statuses are always an icon plus a word, never color alone.
Every vote, duplicate vote and new post is announced through a polite status region; simulated actions say Simulated, nothing was sent.
The similar requests list is linked to the title field with aria-describedby, and each Vote button names the request it votes for.
The voters card is decorative (aria-hidden); the same count is in the vote button's label.
motion: Counts roll only the digits that change, up for a vote and down for an unvote, in tabular numerals so widths never shift.
Sorting moves rows with one 240ms bounce free spring on transform. Rows never reorder on a live vote, so nothing moves under the pointer.
The composer, the similar requests list and a newly posted row open by animating their measured height; everything below glides instead of jumping.
The vote chevron nudges up 3px once when you vote. A new or chosen row gets a brief accent wash.
Footer messages crossfade. With reduced motion, rolls, moves and folds cut to their end state and live votes stop.

name: feedback-board
title: Feedback board
description: A feature request board with a submit form that finds similar requests, upvotes, top and new sorting, status filters, and comments.
whenToUse: A public or in app board where customers suggest and vote on features.
Beta programs that need a lightweight place for requests and team replies.
whenNotToUse: One to one support conversations; use support-conversation or support-widget.
accessibility: The form validates on submit with an inline error tied to the title through aria-describedby and aria-invalid.
Votes are toggle buttons with aria-pressed and a label that names the request and count; changes and posts are announced.
Request titles are buttons with aria-expanded that reveal details and comments in place.
Status always pairs a dot with its name; filters and sort are radiogroups.
motion: Voting hops the arrow and rolls the count. Rows keep their place while you vote and only re-rank when you change sort or filter, so nothing moves under the pointer.
Sort and filter changes glide rows to their new order. A posted request lands at the top with a brief tint.
The form, similar requests, errors, and expanded details open on a critically damped height spring.
Reduced motion removes travel and height springs and keeps short fades.

name: file-upload
title: File upload
description: A complete file selection flow with constraints, progress, and error feedback.
whenToUse: Uploading files with per-file progress, retry, and remove.
Attachments that must be validated by type and size before upload.
Uploads that should abort when a file is removed, via the AbortSignal.
whenNotToUse: Use file-dropzone when you only need to pick files without upload state.
Use import-mapper when uploaded data needs column mapping.
accessibility: The dropzone is role=button with aria-disabled and aria-describedby for the helper text.
An aria-live polite status line announces added, rejected, uploaded, failed, and removed files.
Retry and remove buttons are labelled with the file name.
After removing a file, focus moves to the neighbouring remove button or back to the dropzone.
motion: The dropzone label swaps to Drop to add files while dragging; rows open and close their height on a spring.
One spring drives the progress bar and the counted percentage, the bar folds away once the file lands, and a check draws in.
Reduced motion jumps progress and replaces height and blur swaps with fades.

name: gantt-timeline
title: Gantt timeline
description: A project timeline with draggable, resizable bars, dependency arrows that follow them, and animated zoom.
whenToUse: Planning work across weeks or months where tasks depend on each other.
Roadmaps that people reschedule by dragging, with undo and conflict warnings.
Phase based plans where finished phases can be folded into a summary bar.
whenNotToUse: Use project-board for status columns without dates.
Use week-calendar for time slots within days.
Use timeline for a read-only list of dated events.
accessibility: Bars are role="button" with aria-roledescription "Task bar" or "Milestone", aria-pressed for selection, and a label with name, dates, percent done, and a warning when a dependency is violated.
Every bar is described by hidden text that explains the Alt and Alt Shift shortcuts.
Folded rows are aria-hidden and inert; group toggles carry aria-expanded.
The zoom control is a group of aria-pressed buttons. The footer status is role="status" and reports each change and conflict.
The calendar header, grid lines, arrows, and summary bars are aria-hidden.
motion: Bars, arrows, group summaries, and task rows read the same motion values, so they move together without drifting.
After a drag, the bar springs to the snapped day from its release velocity; a dashed snap target and a date label show while dragging.
Shortening past one day resists with a soft rubber band instead of stopping.
Zoom animates the day scale on a spring while keeping the middle of the view fixed; the header tiers crossfade.
Folding a group slides its rows up into the group row and fades them.
Reduced motion jumps bars, rows, scale, and scroll to their targets and removes the crossfades.

name: goal-tracker
title: Goal tracker
description: A team goals card where objectives open into key results with owners, confidence and progress bars. A weekly check-in updates a value, confidence and note in place, fills the bar and recalculates the objective, and a quarter selector steps from last quarter's final scores to next quarter's planning.
whenToUse: Showing a team's quarterly objectives and key results with owners and confidence.
Collecting a lightweight weekly check-in (value, confidence, note) without leaving the page.
Comparing the active quarter against last quarter's final scores.
whenNotToUse: A single KPI with a trend line; use a metric or stat card.
Task or project tracking with assignees and due dates; use a task list or kanban block.
Org-wide goal trees with parent and child alignment; this card is one level deep.
accessibility: Objectives are disclosure buttons with aria-expanded and aria-controls; collapsed bodies are inert.
Each key result button has a label with its value, target, progress and confidence, so the visual bar is not the only source.
Confidence is always an icon plus a text label, never color alone.
The check-in is a labelled form; the hidden form and hidden key results are inert so focus never lands on invisible controls.
A polite live region announces saves, errors and the recalculated objective, and says when a save was simulated.
motion: Bars fill once when the card first scrolls into view, then tween to new values (560ms ease-out) with percentages counting in tabular numerals.
The objective bar follows its key result 120ms later so cause and effect read clearly.
Key results and the check-in form share one grid cell and crossfade (100ms out, 160ms in), so the card never changes height when the form opens.
Objective bodies open with a bounce-free 240ms spring on measured height; quarters crossfade with an 8px directional shift and the empty state borrows the previous height.
Reduced motion keeps the end states, crossfades and feedback, and drops the fill travel, shifts and the scripted demo.

name: help-center
title: Help center
description: A help center with instant search, topic cards, and popular articles that open into a readable article with an outline and feedback.
whenToUse: A public help center or knowledge base
In-app help with searchable articles
Support portals that deflect tickets with good answers
whenNotToUse: Developer API reference with a nav tree, use docs-sidebar
A short FAQ on a marketing page, use faq-section
Live chat with support, use support-conversation
accessibility: Search is a combobox with a listbox of options and aria-activedescendant; the result count is announced politely.
Articles use real headings; outline links move focus to their section heading and mark the current one with aria-current.
Breadcrumbs are a labelled navigation; the feedback area announces its thank you politely.
Topic icons are decorative; every card is a button named by its text.
motion: Results drop in from the field with a short fade and scale; they are never animated while you arrow through them.
Views slide 16px in the direction of travel, deeper to the right and back to the left.
The outline bar follows the section you are reading on the snappy spring; clicking a section scrolls smoothly.
Feedback states crossfade and the card resizes on the smooth spring. Reduced motion uses fades and instant scrolling.

name: hero-section
title: Hero section
description: Three full screen SaaS heroes: a live dashboard rising from the bottom edge over a drifting mesh, a workflow graph that routes sample events node by node, and editorial type over a mesh gradient.
whenToUse: The first section of a SaaS landing page, when the product screen is the pitch (Screenshot).
Developer tools, automation, and infrastructure products, where showing the product working is the pitch (Workflow).
A launch or download page that wants one confident line and a sense of atmosphere (Mesh).
whenNotToUse: Use page-header for titles inside app screens.
Use hero-signup when the goal is collecting an email in the first section.
accessibility: Each design has one h1, and the calls to action are real links or buttons with visible text.
The dashboard is a labelled group of sample data; its range control is a segmented control and the chart keeps its screen reader table.
The workflow graph is a labelled group; each step's state has a text label (waiting, running, done, skipped) and its result is written out, never shown by color alone.
The mesh and glow are decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Pointer focus draws no ring; keyboard focus shows Arc's shared focus ring.
motion: Screenshot: the copy rises in reading order, then the window rises in behind it and settles flat from a tilt.

Workflow: each step turns to the accent while it runs, the data draws along the edge to the next one, and the result and time swap in with a small spring. The run pauses while the hero is off screen or the tab is hidden.
Mesh: the gradient drifts on the Gradient mesh editor's seamless 20 second loop.

Reduced motion removes every transform: no rise or tilt, the mesh draws one still frame, content fades in briefly, and the workflow shows each event as its finished run without playing; Send test event moves to the next one at once.

name: hero-signup
title: Hero signup
description: A full screen waitlist hero on a soft, drifting mesh gradient: the email field validates as you type and its button grows into the confirmation with your place in line.
whenToUse: Waitlists, early access, and launch pages where the email is the only ask.
Pages that want a calm but alive first impression without product screenshots.
whenNotToUse: Signup that needs a password, SSO choice, or consent up front; use Sign up form.
A newsletter box further down the page; use Newsletter signup.
accessibility: A real form with a labeled type=email field, autocomplete=email, inputmode=email and enterkeyhint=send.

Validation messages are specific (a missing @, an unfinished domain) and tied to the field with aria-describedby and aria-invalid; they appear after blur or submit, never while the first address is still being typed.
Joining, success, and failure are announced through a polite status region; focus moves to the confirmation on success and back to the field on Change email.
The button stays focusable while busy and ignores repeat submits, so a double press never joins twice.
The field font is 16px on phones so iOS never zooms, and every target is at least 44px tall.
motion: The headline rises in word by word once on load, followed by the supporting line, the field, and the social proof.
Submitting crossfades the label into a spinner inside the same button, so nothing changes size.
Success is one spatial transition: the button's shape grows across the whole field on a critically damped spring and becomes the confirmation, while the place in line rolls in digit by digit.

The mesh drifts on a slow, seamless loop and blends into the new colors when the theme or accent changes. Reduced motion draws one still frame, removes the rise, the shake and the rolls, and swaps states instantly.

name: horizon-chart
title: Horizon chart
description: A horizon chart that stacks fourteen daily series as compact folded rows, with a synced crosshair, a sort by name, peak or latest, a band count setting that folds every row on one spring, and a legend that explains how to read the bands.
whenToUse: Operations or growth dashboards comparing many markets, services or products against their own baseline over weeks or months.
Monitoring views where the reader scans for which rows broke from normal and when, then reads exact values on one day.
Any time series comparison where small multiples of line charts would need too much height.
whenNotToUse: Use small-multiples when there are only a few series and the reader needs axes and exact levels in each panel.
Use ridgeline to compare distributions rather than values over time.
Use streamgraph to show how parts add up to a total over time.
Use line-chart for one to four series that should be read precisely against a y axis.
accessibility: The chart is a focusable group with a keyboard hint; focusing it places the crosshair on the latest day.
A visually hidden table lists every row with its latest value, its highest and its lowest value with their dates, in the current order.
Moving the crosshair by keyboard announces the day with the highest and lowest row through one polite live region; sort and band changes are announced there too.
Values carry a sign and the legend names both sides (below and above), so direction never depends on color alone. The color scale is an image with a full text label.
Pointer focus draws no ring; keyboard focus shows Arc's shared focus ring. Keyboard position shows as the crosshair, the readout and the selected fills of the switches.
motion: Changing the band count animates one motion value that drives two custom properties on the root, so every layer in every row folds or unfolds together on a no-overshoot spring, on transform and opacity alone.
Sorting moves each row to its new place with a layout spring that never overshoots.
The crosshair is a full-width track translated by a share of its own width, following the pointer on a short critically damped spring; it appears in place instead of sliding in from its last day.
Row values and the date are written straight to the DOM while scrubbing, so the pointer never renders React.
Reduced motion makes the fold, the reorder and the crosshair instant.

name: login-immersive
title: Immersive login
description: A glass magic link card over dusk photography that folds its envelope shut once sent.
whenToUse: A magic link sign in page with a strong brand photo behind a glass card.
Consumer or creative products where the sign in screen carries the brand mood.
whenNotToUse: Use login-centered for passkey-first auth with an email code.
Use login-split for password sign in with a quieter layout.
Use sign-in when the form sits inside an existing page.
accessibility: The email field uses autoComplete="email" and SSO buttons sit in a labelled role="group".
Busy actions use aria-disabled rather than disabled so focus is kept.
A polite role="status" region announces when the link is sent and resend availability.
motion: After sending, the form gives way to an envelope that folds shut and the resend countdown rolls.
Reduced motion replaces the fold and slides with fades.

name: inbox-sidebar
title: Inbox sidebar
description: A mail sidebar whose Compose button grows into a composer and whose folders take dropped mail.
whenToUse: The shell of a mail or messaging app.
Inboxes where messages are dragged onto folders.
Mail clients with row quick actions and a compose window.
whenNotToUse: Use inbox-triage for a focused one-at-a-time triage flow.
Use notification-center for app notifications.
Use workspace-sidebar for general app navigation.
accessibility: The composer is a role="dialog" labelled by its title.
Moves, stars, and sends are announced through a polite status region, and rail icons have tooltips.
Every drag action has a keyboard or menu alternative.
motion: Compose grows into the composer through a shared layoutId, and unread counts roll.
Dropped messages leave the list with layout animation while the target folder pulses.
Reduced motion makes the morph and list changes instant.

name: inbox-triage
title: Inbox triage
description: Process a focused inbox with archive, snooze, and restore actions.
whenToUse: A queue of messages or requests that need archive, snooze, or restore decisions.
Inboxes where rows expand in place to show details and actions.
whenNotToUse: Use inbox-sidebar for mail navigation with folders and counts.
Use notification-center for system notifications.
Use swipe-actions for touch-first lists with gesture actions.
accessibility: Folders are a tablist with arrow key navigation; the list is its tabpanel.
Message rows toggle with aria-expanded and aria-controls and declare their shortcuts with aria-keyshortcuts.
After a message leaves, focus moves to the next row, or to the heading when the list is empty; undo returns focus to the restored row.
Moves are announced in a polite role="status" region; the Unread filter uses aria-pressed.
motion: Rows and message details open and collapse with height and opacity on the smooth spring.
The folder indicator glides between tabs with a shared layoutId; the status line swaps with a short rise.
Reduced motion removes height and travel and keeps plain fades.

name: integrations
title: Integrations
description: An integrations directory where Connect morphs to Connected and the filters recount as you go.
whenToUse: Settings or marketplace pages for third party connections.
Directories with search, category filters, and Connect buttons.
Connections that need sync settings and a safe disconnect.
whenNotToUse: Use webhooks for outgoing event endpoints.
Use api-keys for developer credentials.
accessibility: Filters are a role="radiogroup" of role="radio" buttons with aria-checked and roving arrow keys.
Filter results and connection changes are announced in a polite status region.
Disconnect uses hold to confirm, so it cannot fire from a stray click.
motion: Connect morphs into a Connected state and filter counts recount as you go.
Cards reflow with layout animation when filtering.
Reduced motion swaps morphs and reflow for instant changes.

name: invite-people
title: Invite people
description: Invite teammates with roles, bulk paste validation, a seat meter, and avatars that fly into a pending list.
whenToUse: Inviting several people at once by name or email, with a role for each.
Plans with a seat limit where people should see the effect of an invite before sending.
Flows where users paste a messy list from a spreadsheet and need clear per-entry errors.
whenNotToUse: Use team-members to manage people who already joined.
Use roles-permissions to edit what each role can do.
Use tag-input for a plain chip field without a directory, roles, or seats.
accessibility: The field is a combobox with aria-expanded, aria-controls, and aria-activedescendant pointing into a role="listbox" of options; blocked options are aria-disabled.
Role menus are role="menu" with menuitemradio items and aria-checked.
The seat bar is a role="meter" with aria-valuetext such as "12 of 10 seats, 2 over the limit".
Send stays focusable with aria-disabled while blocked and points aria-describedby at the error list or the seat summary.
Every add, remove, send, join, and revoke is announced in a polite live region.
motion: Avatars share layoutIds, so a person flies from the suggestion into a chip, from the chip into the pending list, and from the row into the team stack when they join.
Invalid chips shake when you try to send; the over-limit notice shakes on the same attempt.
Labels that change length resize on a spring and crossfade their text; the field height springs as chips wrap.
Reduced motion (MotionConfig reducedMotion="user" plus a hydrated flag) removes shakes, offsets, and layout travel and sets durations to zero.

name: invoice-studio
title: Invoice studio
description: An editable invoice with live totals and a clear save flow.
whenToUse: Creating or editing an invoice or quote with line items.
Forms that need a live subtotal and total as quantities and rates change.
whenNotToUse: Use billing-overview to show past invoices and plan status.
Use checkout-flow when the customer is paying.
Use sortable-data-table for read-only lists of invoices.
accessibility: The total is an output element with aria-live and aria-atomic.
Save progress and validation messages are announced via role="status".
Row inputs and remove buttons carry per-line aria-labels.
motion: Totals roll with a short vertical slide and blur when they change.
Added and removed lines animate height via layout.
Reduced motion uses opacity-only swaps with zero duration.

name: journey-flow
title: Journey flow
description: A Sankey of user journeys whose flows morph by channel and trace a cohort on hover.
whenToUse: Showing where users go between funnel stages, such as visit to signup to activation.
Comparing flows across acquisition channels with a segment switch.
Tracing one step to see which paths lead into and out of it.
whenNotToUse: Use cohort-retention to show how groups retain over time.
Use bar-chart for a simple linear funnel without branching paths.
Use metrics-dashboard for a general KPI overview.
accessibility: Segments form a role="radiogroup"; steps sit in a role="toolbar" with roving tabIndex and aria-pressed.
The diagram is role="img" with a text summary; each step button's label includes its users and share of visitors.
A polite live region announces visits and paid plans when the channel changes.
The breakdown panel is a labelled aside, and the data table toggle exposes aria-expanded for a non-visual reading of the chart.
motion: Ribbons morph their widths on a spring slightly slower than a control when the segment changes; counts follow a beat later and never overshoot.
Tracing dims everything outside the cohort; panel text settles with a short rise and digits roll in place.
Reduced motion swaps the morph for an instant change with an opacity fade.

name: kanban-board
title: Kanban board
description: A kanban board where cards lift, tilt and spring into the slot that opens for them, with swimlanes and live WIP limits.
whenToUse: A team board where cards move between statuses.
Pipelines where ordering within a stage matters.
Boards that need a per person view.
whenNotToUse: Scheduling on dates; use gantt-timeline or week-calendar.
Read only status summaries; use a table.
Hundreds of cards per column; virtualize or use customers-table.
accessibility: Cards are focusable buttons with a draggable role description and a label that includes title, id and assignee.
Every pick up, move and drop is announced in an assertive live region with the column and position.
The drawer is a modal dialog: focus moves in, Tab is trapped, Escape closes it and focus returns to the card.
WIP limits are shown with text as well as color.
motion: The lifted card rides pointer motion values, lifts slightly and tilts on a spring from horizontal velocity.
Neighbours glide aside with layout springs as the slot moves; on release a small spring chases the slot's live position and carries the throw velocity.
Switching to swimlanes flies every card to its lane with shared layout ids.
Reduced motion drops tilt and travel; drops land at once.

name: knowledge-base
title: Knowledge base
description: A retrieval knowledge base in one card: add sources and watch them parse, chunk, embed and index, then test a question and see which chunks come back and why.
whenToUse: Admin screens for a RAG or support assistant where people add documents, watch them index, and check what a question retrieves.
Explaining or tuning chunking, hybrid search and reranking with a working test bench instead of a diagram.
Debugging why an assistant answered from the wrong source by looking at scores, matches and neighbouring chunks.
whenNotToUse: Use vector-search to illustrate how embeddings and nearest neighbours work; this block is the working product surface.
Use document-extract to pull structured fields out of a single document.
Use agent-memory to show what an agent remembers about a user or a project.
Use ai-answer or research-run to show the cited answer a model writes from retrieved sources.
accessibility: The card is a labelled section. Each pipeline is a progressbar with the overall percent and a value text that names the step, such as Embed, step 3 of 4, or Failed at embed.
Status never relies on color: indexed rows show a check with a label, failed rows an alert icon with the reason in text, and working rows a named step and a percent.
Each result is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls; its similarity or reranker score and any rank change (for example, Up 2 after reranking, was 3) are in its accessible name.
Matching words are wrapped in mark elements, so assistive technology can report highlighted text.
Ingestion milestones, failures, search results, reranking and simulated actions are announced through one polite status region; simulated uploads say that files stay in the browser.
Icon-only controls (settings, clear query) have specific names. The settings toggles are full labels, so the text toggles the switch too.
Pointer focus draws no ring; keyboard focus shows Arc's shared focus ring.
motion: Turning on Rerank shows a short reranking state, then moves each result to its new rank with a critically damped layout animation (no bounce) while score bars and numbers roll to the reranker's values and a rank change fades in.
Opening a result springs its height open: the previous chunk slides in above, the excerpt grows from two lines to the full chunk, and the next chunk slides in below, all on the smooth spring.
Pipeline segments fill from a single animation-frame clock while counts climb; the meta line crossfades when a step changes. Active labels use a finite text shimmer that settles when the step ends.
New sources open in at the top of the list on a height spring; removed ones close their gap. Views crossfade without moving.
Reduced motion places results, heights and values immediately, stops the spinner and the skeleton pulse, and keeps every label and announcement.

name: kpi-drilldown
title: KPI drilldown
description: KPI cards that expand into a full detail chart with period comparison and a breakdown table, then fold back.
whenToUse: An analytics or finance overview where each number deserves a closer look.
Executive dashboards that compare the current period with the previous one.
whenNotToUse: Use metric-explorer to compare many metrics on one chart.
Use metrics-dashboard for a static summary without drill down.
Avoid it for real time monitoring where values change every second.
accessibility: Cards are buttons whose name includes the value and the change.
The detail is a labeled region; the grid behind it is hidden from assistive technology while it is open.
The chart has a spoken summary and a keyboard cursor; changes pair an arrow and sign with color.
Breakdowns are real tables with row headers.
motion: The card grows into the detail on one spring, and the detail folds back into the same card.
Every range is resampled to the same number of points, so sparklines and the detail line morph instead of redrawing.
Values roll digit by digit when the range changes.
The previous period line fades in and out with Compare; breakdown rows crossfade and their share bars fill with a small stagger.
Reduced motion jumps between grid and detail and keeps short fades.

name: layout-morph
title: Layout morph
description: A 24 card gallery that flies between grid, masonry, list, fan, carousel and a 3D helix.
whenToUse: Catalogue, portfolio, or team pages where people browse the same set in different layouts.
Showcase galleries that fly between grid, masonry, list, fan, carousel, and a 3D helix.
whenNotToUse: Use photo-grid for a simple gallery.
Use carousel or cover-flow for one horizontal browsing style.
Use lightbox-gallery when opening a full size image is the main job.
accessibility: The view switch is a role="radiogroup" with roving tabindex and labelled icon options.
The stage is a group with a gallery roledescription whose label explains the keys.
The open card is a role="dialog"; the gallery behind it is hidden and the closed dialog is inert.
motion: Cards fly between layouts on springs, staggered outward from the chosen origin.
Opening a card morphs it into the detail view.
Reduced motion is passed to the engine and MotionConfig uses the user setting.

name: lead-scoring
title: Lead scoring
description: A lead scoring card where inbound B2B leads are ranked by an AI fit score, each with a score ring and a one-line reason. Open a lead to see its signals and score breakdown, then push it to HubSpot or Salesforce.
whenToUse: A sales inbox or SDR queue that ranks new inbound leads by fit.
Showing why a model scored a lead, with signals and a weighted breakdown.
Handing a qualified lead to HubSpot or Salesforce from the same view.
whenNotToUse: Large tables of hundreds of leads with filters and bulk edits; use a data table.
Enriching columns of company data; use enrich-column.
Tracking the health of existing customers; use account-health.
accessibility: Each row is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls; its label reads name, title, company, score, fit band and the reason.
The score ring is decorative; the number and the fit band are in the row label and the breakdown list label.
Status is never color alone: done and error states pair an icon with a short label.
The CRM picker is a radio group with roving focus and named options.
A polite live region announces pushes, errors and rescoring, and says when a push was simulated.
motion: Re-sorting glides each row to its new place with a bounce-free spring (position only, text is never scaled).
The ring arc and number share one motion value, so they count up together in about 640ms with tabular numerals.
Opening a row springs the measured height with no bounce; breakdown bars grow with a 30ms stagger.
Time, synced, reason and status swaps are single crossfades in a fixed slot, so nothing changes size.
The scoring spinner pauses off screen. Reduced motion keeps every end state and drops travel, counting and the spinner.

name: line-replay
title: Line replay
description: A time replay line chart that draws a day of traffic with a moving playhead, a value label on the tip, a scrubber, speed control and key moments annotated as the playhead passes them.
whenToUse: Post-launch or campaign reviews where the team wants to watch traffic respond to each announcement.
Incident retrospectives that step through a metric with the alert, the deploy and the recovery marked.
Storytelling pages and reports where a single series over one session or day is best understood in sequence.
whenNotToUse: Use annotated-trend when people need to add and edit their own notes on a static trend.
Use connected-scatter to replay how two measures moved together over time.
Use metric-explorer or a line chart to compare several series or ranges at a glance without playback.
accessibility: The scrubber is a role="slider" measured in minutes; its value text reads the time and the value ("9:40 am, 2,316 on site") and is updated whenever playback is paused, so a screen reader is not flooded while it plays.

The readout above the chart repeats the time, the value, the ratio to the comparison and the peak so far as text, so nothing is available only as a line position. The drawing itself is hidden from assistive technology.
Passing a moment during playback, pausing, jumping and finishing are announced through a polite live region ("9:40 am. Hacker News front page.", "Replay finished. Peak 6,041 at 10:25 am.").
Key moments are an ordered list of buttons; the latest reached one has aria-current. A moment's effect line stays hidden from screen readers until the replay has played through it.
The play button has a specific name for each state: Play replay, Pause replay, Replay from the start.

Incidents carry a warning icon and their own title, never color alone. Pointer focus draws no ring; keyboard focus shows Arc's shared focus ring. The scrubber and the moment rows show keyboard position with a fill.
motion: Playback advances a single motion value from requestAnimationFrame; each frame writes the line and area paths, the playhead, the tip label, the axis clock, the scrubber and the readout straight to the DOM. React renders only when a moment is passed, playback starts or stops, or the size changes.
Replay and jumping to a moment glide the playhead with the smooth spring, which never overshoots, so the line retracts or extends to the target and a new jump mid-way picks up from where it is.

Passing a moment settles its marker onto the line (opacity and scale), fades in its stem, and rises its callout into the lane above the plot on the smooth spring; the previous callout fades out faster than the new one enters.
Time axis labels fade out of the way of the playhead clock instead of overlapping it.
Reduced motion keeps playback (it is started by the viewer and can be paused at any time) but makes rewinds, jumps, markers and callouts instant and turns off autoplay.

name: checkout-live
title: Live checkout
description: A subscription checkout whose summary recomputes as you edit, then glides to the centre and unfolds into a receipt.
whenToUse: Upgrade from a free plan to a paid team plan.
Paid signup where seats and add-ons change the price.
A self serve checkout that needs coupons and tax by country.
whenNotToUse: A physical goods cart with shipping; use checkout-flow.
Only showing totals without payment; use checkout-summary.
Comparing plans before choosing; use plan-comparison.
accessibility: Plans and billing period are radio groups with aria-checked; add-ons are real checkboxes.
Errors are tied to their inputs with aria-describedby and aria-invalid, and a failed submit focuses the first invalid field.
Rolling amounts keep the full value in visually hidden text, so screen readers never hear single digits.
On success focus moves to the receipt heading; payment errors use role alert.
motion: Every amount rolls digit by digit on the snappy spring; add-on and discount lines open and close their height on the smooth spring.
On success the form fades aside and the summary glides to the centre with one position spring, while the coupon folds away and receipt details unfold.
The selected plan ring and billing pill travel between options as shared layout highlights.
Reduced motion keeps every state and swaps travel for instant changes.

name: login-split
title: Login split
description: A full screen split login: an email-first form that morphs into a password step beside a photo.
whenToUse: Password-based sign in with an email-first step beside a brand photo.
Sign in pages that should show the recognised account before asking for a password.
whenNotToUse: Use login-centered for passkey-first auth.
Use login-immersive for magic link auth.
Use signup-form for account creation.
accessibility: Fields use autoComplete="username" and "current-password"; errors render in a role="alert" tied with aria-describedby and aria-invalid.
SSO buttons sit in a labelled role="group".
A polite role="status" region announces step changes and simulated link actions.
motion: Continue morphs the email form into the password step with the account avatar, and labels roll between states.
Reduced motion uses fades and shortens the simulated delays.

examples.title: Real links
examples.code:
<LoginSplit
  fullScreen
  links={{ signUp: "/sign-up", terms: "/terms", privacy: "/privacy" }}
  onSignIn={account => router.push("/app")}
/>

name: logo-marquee
title: Logo marquee
description: A quiet, continuously moving row of brand marks with a pause control.
whenToUse: A customer or integration logo strip on a landing page.
Social proof sections with a heading and a short supporting line.
whenNotToUse: Use integrations when each logo needs a description or a connect action.
Use testimonial-stage when quotes matter more than logos.
Use carousel when people should browse items by hand.
accessibility: The duplicated loop copy is aria-hidden, so each brand is read once.
The pause button uses aria-pressed and a live region announces the motion state.
motion: A CSS keyframe loop scrolls two copies of the list for a seamless track.
Under prefers-reduced-motion the animation stops and the duplicate list is hidden.

examples.title: Integration logos
examples.code:
<LogoMarquee
  title="Works with your stack"
  description="Connect the tools your team already uses."
  brands={[
    { name: "Linear", icon: "/logos/linear.svg" },
    { name: "Figma", icon: "/logos/figma.svg" },
    { name: "Notion", icon: "/logos/notion.svg" },
  ]}
/>

name: magic-link
title: Magic link
description: A passwordless sign in card where an email with inline validation and typo fixes sends a magic link, and the card crossfades in place to a check your inbox step with a sealing envelope, Gmail and Outlook shortcuts and a resend countdown. Google and GitHub sign in sit above, with their real marks.
whenToUse: Passwordless sign in or sign up by email link, with optional Google and GitHub sign in.
B2B products that want a work email gate with a clear what happens next screen.
Replacing a password form to cut sign in friction and reset requests.
whenNotToUse: Password plus email sign in or MFA codes; use sign-in or a login block instead.
One time codes typed into the app; use an OTP input flow.
Full page marketing sign in layouts with imagery; use login-split.
accessibility: The card is a labelled region ("Sign in to Halden"); the hidden step is inert, so it leaves the tab order and the accessibility tree.
Focus follows the step: the Check your inbox heading takes focus when the link is sent, and Use a different email returns focus to the field with the address selected.
The field has a real label, autocomplete="email" and an email keyboard on touch. Errors set aria-invalid, are linked with aria-describedby and announced as alerts, and carry an icon as well as color.
A polite live region announces sends, resends and simulated actions ("Simulated, nothing was sent").
Resend stays focusable during the countdown (aria-disabled), so focus never drops when a resend starts.
motion: Steps crossfade in one grid cell: the old step fades out in 100ms, the new one fades in over 200ms with a 4px rise. Nothing resizes.
The envelope plays once per send in about 0.8s: the letter drops in, the flap folds shut, a success check settles. It replays on every resend. No bounce, no loop.
Messages under the field and resend labels swap with a single opacity crossfade inside reserved space; the countdown digits change in place in tabular numerals.
Reduced motion drops the rise and the envelope travel and renders its sealed end state, keeping the crossfades short.

name: market-terminal
title: Market terminal
description: A trading terminal with a canvas candlestick chart, volume, moving averages, crosshair OHLC readout, wheel, drag and pinch zoom, a live watchlist with sparklines and flashing prices, and a market and limit order ticket.
whenToUse: A trading or investing product that needs a full chart, a watchlist and an order ticket on one screen.
A paper trading or education app where people practice placing market and limit orders against moving prices.
A markets dashboard where candles, volume and moving averages must be inspected bar by bar.
whenNotToUse: Use order-book-depth to show bids and asks at each price level.
Use metric-explorer or a line chart for product or business metrics without open, high, low and close.
Use options-payoff to model an options position's profit at expiry.
Use wallet-card for a simple balance and recent transactions without a chart.
accessibility: The chart is a focusable image with a role description, a label naming the symbol, range and candle interval, and a description of its keys.
Moving the crosshair with the keyboard announces the candle's time, open, high, low, close, change and volume through a polite live region.
Watchlist rows are buttons with a full label (ticker, name, price and change today); the charted symbol carries aria-current.
Direction is never color alone: changes carry a sign and an arrow, and order status is written as text.
Order problems (too few shares, not enough buying power, not enough shares to sell) and failures are written in a status line under the button.
Pointer focus draws no ring; keyboard focus shows Arc's shared focus ring. Keyboard position shows as a fill on rows, toggles and icon buttons, and as the crosshair on the chart.
motion: The chart is one canvas drawn in a requestAnimationFrame loop that runs only while something moves; React never re-renders per frame.
Zoom, pan and range changes ease the view and the price scale with an exponential approach timed from the smooth spring, so nothing overshoots and every gesture can be reversed mid-way.
A drag flick carries momentum that decays like a thrown card. Pinch zooms around the midpoint of two fingers.
Live ticks glide the last candle, its price tag, the price line and the moving averages to the new price; the header price rolls with the animated counter.
Each watchlist price flashes a green or red tint in the direction it moved, as a single opacity fade. The selected row's fill glides between rows.
The limit field opens with height and opacity together; new orders grow into the list. The live dot's pulse is the only loop, because it reports live status.
Reduced motion makes the view, prices and panels change at once, drops momentum and the pulse, and holds the flash as a brief static tint.

name: mcp-servers
title: MCP servers
description: Manage the MCP servers that give an agent its tools: see what the enabled tools cost in context, connect or pause a server, and switch single tools on or off.
whenToUse: Settings for an agent or AI assistant that connects to MCP servers: which servers it has, which tools are on and what they cost in context.
Onboarding a new integration with a directory, sign in and tool discovery in one place.
Keeping tool definitions inside a context budget by switching off tools the agent does not need.
whenNotToUse: Use agent-approvals to approve or deny individual tool calls while the agent runs.
Use context-window to show everything in the context window, not only tool definitions.
Use agent-run to follow an agent's steps and tool calls live.
Use knowledge-base to manage documents an agent retrieves from, rather than tools it calls.
accessibility: Each server row is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, named with the server, its status, transport, tools on and token cost.

Status is an icon in its semantic color plus a word (Connected, Needs sign in, Error, Connecting), never color alone. Read and write tools carry an eye or pen icon and the word; below 400px the word stays for screen readers only.
The context bar is a meter with a value text such as "6,400 of 8,000 budgeted tokens", and over budget adds how far over it is beside a warning icon.
Every tool switch is named with the tool, its access and its token cost, and the tool name is its label, so clicking the name toggles it.
The sheet is a modal dialog: the card behind it is inert, Tab is trapped inside, Escape closes it, and focus moves to the search field, the Authorize button or the step heading as the flow advances.
Toggles, permission changes, connects, failures, removes and undo are announced in a polite status region, and the simulated authorize screen says plainly that no account is contacted.
When a row's action button disappears (Retry, Sign in) or a row is removed, focus moves to that row or its neighbour so keyboard users never land on the page body.
Pointer focus draws no ring; keyboard focus shows Arc's shared focus ring.
motion: Toggling a tool rolls the tool count and token numbers with tabular digits, and its server's segment resizes on a critically damped spring.
Hovering or focusing a server highlights its segment in the first series color and dims the others.
Rows open and close their tools on a smooth height spring with a short fade; the chevron turns.
The sheet rises from the card's bottom edge over a scrim, without overshoot. Steps cross fade with an 18px shift in the direction of the flow.
Discovered tools arrive one by one with a 4px fade in, under a calm shimmer on "Discovering tools" that settles into "Found 5 tools".
A new server slides into the top of the list as its height opens, with a brief accent tint that fades out. Removed rows close their gap, and Undo opens them again in place.
Status labels and actions cross fade (about 100ms out, 160ms in). No text morphs or per letter motion.
Reduced motion drops travel, height animation and the shimmer: content appears in place with every state, focus move and announcement kept.

name: media-player
title: Media player
description: An audio player with a living playlist and complete playback controls.
whenToUse: A small audio collection such as a podcast, sample pack, or playlist.
Pages that need a full player with seek, skip, volume, and a track list.
whenNotToUse: Use now-playing for a compact now playing widget.
Use transcript-studio when the audio needs a synced transcript.
Use voice-recorder for recording audio.
accessibility: Uses a native audio element with range inputs for seek and volume.
Transport and playlist buttons have labels such as "Play <title>" and "Next track"; the current track has aria-current.
Seek and volume ranges carry aria-valuetext such as "0:12 of 0:24" and "70%". The mute button's label switches between Mute and Unmute audio.
motion: The selection rail glides to the current track with a shared layoutId on the gentle spring; playing bars pulse beside it.
The cover crossfades and the title rises in when the track changes; the play icon swaps with a short scale and blur.
Reduced motion removes the glides, swaps, and bar animation.

name: metric-explorer
title: Metric explorer
description: KPI cards that open into a scrubbable chart and morph between metrics and ranges.
whenToUse: The top of a SaaS analytics or finance page with KPI cards that open into a chart.
Dashboards where people move between a few metrics and date ranges.
whenNotToUse: Use stat-card or metric-card for static KPI tiles.
Use revenue-explorer for a revenue breakdown with a range brush.
Use metrics-dashboard for a full dashboard layout.
accessibility: Each card is a button whose label reads the value, change and range.
The open chart uses a tablist and tabpanel, and the scrubber is a role="slider" with a dated aria-valuetext.
The close button advertises Escape with aria-keyshortcuts, and a polite live region announces changes.
motion: A card's surface morphs into the chart panel with a shared layout transition and back on close.
The line morphs between metrics and ranges, and the tab highlight slides with the selection.
Reduced motion replaces the morph and slides with instant changes.

name: metrics-dashboard
title: Metrics dashboard
description: A dense analytics view with KPI tabs, one inspectable chart, and top pages and sources.
whenToUse: A small, explorable KPI overview with a range toggle and one chart.
Product or marketing dashboards with four headline metrics, a 7, 30, or 90 day range, and top pages and sources.
whenNotToUse: Use metric-explorer or revenue-explorer for larger or drill-down data.
Use stat-card for a single number.
Use sparkline for inline trends in a table.
accessibility: Range buttons use aria-pressed; the KPI tiles are tabs with aria-selected.
The chart is role="img" with a label; the inspected value is announced through a status tooltip.
Deltas carry a text direction, not only color.
motion: KPI values and list counts count to their new amounts with tabular numerals.
The range thumb and KPI underline slide on a spring; the chart crossfades between metrics and ranges.
Reduced motion swaps values and views immediately.

name: model-arena
title: Model arena
description: A blind side by side model comparison in one card: send one prompt to two models, watch both answers stream at the same pace, vote for the better one, then reveal which model wrote each.
whenToUse: Blind human preference tests between two models on the same prompt, such as an internal bake-off before switching providers.
Prompt or model evaluation tools where people should judge answers without knowing which model wrote them.
Showing latency, speed and cost differences between two models live, side by side, on a real prompt.
whenNotToUse: Use model-picker to let someone choose one model for their own chat; this block compares answers, it does not set a default.
Use eval-suite to score many prompts automatically against expected outputs rather than collecting one human vote at a time.
Use model-router to explain or configure automatic routing between models.
Use ai-chat for a single ongoing conversation with one model.
accessibility: Each pane is a labelled region ("Model A", or "Model A, Claude Opus 5.5" once revealed). Its answer is a focusable scroll region marked aria-busy while it streams.
In blind mode no model name, mark or title reaches the page or the accessibility tree until the vote.
Every status pairs an icon with a word: Thinking, Writing, Done, Finished first, Stopped, Failed. Color only reinforces it.

A polite status region narrates the round: that a run started (and that the preview is simulated), which model finished first, that voting is open, the vote result with both real models, and a leaderboard reset.
On narrow containers the panes use tab semantics: a tablist with aria-selected tabs, each controlling a tabpanel; the hidden panel leaves the tab order.

The vote buttons form a labelled group. Leaderboard rows read their rank and win rate as text, the bars are hidden from assistive technology, and the Leaderboard button's name says when a vote has updated it.
Run carries aria-keyshortcuts for its shortcut. Pointer focus draws no ring; keyboard focus shows Arc's shared focus ring, inset inside scroll regions.
motion: Answers stream in chunks of whole words every 30 to 40ms, each fading in over 160ms with no blur or travel, at the same pace in both panes; settled text never re-renders, and each answer follows its stream until the reader scrolls up.

The reveal is one minimal crossfade: "Model A" fades out in 100ms while the brand mark and name fade in over 160ms from 2px below, and the label's measured width follows on a spring with no bounce. Status words and tab labels swap the same way; no character morph, blur or per letter motion anywhere.
Working statuses shimmer with Text shimmer, and each status word mounts with its own shimmer so a change is a crossfade, never a morph inside the label.
First token time counts live while the model thinks; speed and cost are sampled twice a second while it writes and roll on Animated counter digits, so each roll settles before the next.
The vote row crossfades between waiting, voting and result while its height follows on the smooth spring. Run and Stop share one cell, so the button never changes width.

Opening the leaderboard after a vote replays it: rows start at their earlier ranks and glide to the new ones on a critically damped spring while win rates roll and bars scale in each model's series color; ranks stay put while rows move. After the first vote, the bars grow from empty.
Narrow tabs slide their highlight on a 220ms tween with no bounce, and the chosen pane fades in.
Reduced motion keeps every state, label and announcement but shows chunks without fading, swaps labels instantly, reorders rows in place and stops the spinner and shimmer.

name: model-picker
title: Model picker
description: A model picker in one quiet pill: open it to choose from featured models with a one line note each, set the reasoning effort, or browse every other model by provider, and the pill swaps to your choice in place.
whenToUse: Choosing the model and effort for a chat, an agent or a playground.
A default model setting with a short review of what the chosen model costs and how much context it takes.
whenNotToUse: Comparing two models' answers side by side; use model-arena.
A full prompt box with attachments and tools; use ai-composer, which has its own model chip.
Choosing from a plain list of options with no descriptions; use the select or dropdown-menu component.
